#!/bin/zsh
# bench.sh <csv> <repo_dir> <label> <timeout_s> <runs> -- cmd...
csv=$1; repo=$2; label=$3; tmo=$4; runs=$5; shift 6
for i in $(seq 1 $runs); do
  out=$(cd "$repo" && { /usr/bin/time -p perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' $tmo "$@" > /tmp/bench_out.$$ 2>/tmp/bench_err.$$; } 2>&1; echo "exit=$?")
  rc=$(echo "$out" | grep -o 'exit=[0-9]*' | cut -d= -f2)
  t=$(grep -E '^real' /tmp/bench_err.$$ 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}')
  [ -z "$t" ] && t=$(echo "$out" | grep -E '^real' | awk '{print $2}')
  bytes=$(wc -c < /tmp/bench_out.$$ | tr -d ' ')
  echo "$label,$i,$t,$rc,$bytes" >> "$csv"
  echo "RUN $label #$i real=${t}s exit=$rc out_bytes=$bytes"
done
rm -f /tmp/bench_out.$$ /tmp/bench_err.$$

All benchmarking and root-cause work is complete. Full data is in `.context/bench/results.csv`; findings are recorded as durable Brain facts. Here's the ranked list.

## Ranked performance problems

All slow paths scale with **retained checkpoint/session volume**, not repo size — a 12GB repo with no sessions cold-indexes in 28s, while this repo's 337-transcript/1.5GB store makes "cheap" commands take a minute. Everything was measured on real stores across 5 states (big-indexed, un-indexed, fresh-small, fresh-medium, stale), with root causes confirmed in source.

**1. `status` takes 60–72s, every run (also `brain_status` over MCP: 72s)** — the worst because it's the entry point everything tells agents to run, and 72s blows past typical 60s MCP tool timeouts. `brief` proves the base report costs 0.3s; the rest is `populateBrainStatusVerification` loading the *entire* checkpoint store: one serial `git ls-tree` per checkpoint ref plus one `git cat-file` per metadata blob (`internal/cli/export.go:1705-2800`). A metadata cache exists (`export/checkpoint-metadata-cache.json.gz`) but this path passes `nil` for it (`verify_cmd.go:798`) — wiring it in is nearly a one-line fix. Snapshot assembly is also O(checkpoints × tree-paths) (`export.go:2062`). Fix: pass the cache, batch blobs through one `git cat-file --batch`, scope the snapshot to the 10 sampled facts' checkpoints.

**2. `verify` takes 334s for 1211 facts** — per anchor it runs `git for-each-ref --contains` (an O(history) walk, memoized only per commit, and each fact tends to have its own commit) plus **two full transcript reads with no memoization** — ~10GB of redundant I/O since facts share sessions (`verify_cmd.go:381-523,674`). Fix: batch reachability once for all distinct commits, memoize transcripts on the context, compare digests instead of full bytes.

**3. `refresh delta` takes 39–47s even when there's nothing to do** — this is your "slow indexing at startup," since hooks/watch run delta routinely. It reads and SHA-256s the whole 1.5GB corpus *before* the size+mtime cache check can short-circuit, because the check requires the digest it was supposed to avoid computing (`history_delta.go:307-334`, `history.go:1449`). Fix: hash only when size/mtime differ. The export half is fine (`refresh sessions` alone: 0.8s).

**4. `refresh history` takes 48s and always rebuilds all 168k records** — it hashes the corpus twice more, and materializes the 113MB index roughly four times (`MarshalIndent`, three separate hashes, per-record re-marshal for the fingerprint) (`history.go:363-431`). The only skip-guard re-hashes the corpus a third time. Side effect: the first read of the 113MB index makes the next `brief` spike to 5.7s (0.4s warm). Fix: stream-encode once through a MultiWriter computing both digests; derive fingerprints from cached per-file digests.

**5. `entities history` takes 61s to return nothing** — every path through `loadEntityIndexView` runs the same full checkpoint scan as #1 (again with `nil` cache), even when the entity index is empty because the graph plugin is missing; plus a wasted 10s-timeout `entire graph version` probe (`entities_cmd.go:591-868`). Fix: early-return on empty index; scope the snapshot to referenced checkpoints.

**6. Amplifier: every git call spawns a second, uncached `git config` probe** (`runner.go:88`, `git_harden_filters.go:85-124`), doubling the fork bill on findings 1/2/5 — ~27s of the status run is sys time from fork/exec. It's also the one spawn with no `WaitDelay`. A per-invocation memo halves process count everywhere at once.

**7. Semantic indexing couldn't be measured here** — `refresh index`, `repair`, and `entities backfill` all fail because entire-graph isn't installed on this machine, so the historically recorded worst offender (provider snapshot timing out at 900s, per Brain's own recall) is unverified in this audit. Worth a follow-up run on a machine with the graph plugin.

## What's already fast (no action)

`query` all modes ~0.2s, `brief` 0.35s, `recall` 0.24s, `get`/`multi-get`, `stats`, `doctor`, `gc`, `remember`, `facts vitality`, `overview`, `docs`, MCP initialize/tools-list/query (0.1–0.2s). Un-indexed repos fail fast (0.2s). Cold non-semantic indexing is fine: 4s small / 5s medium / 28s for the 12GB repo. History generations are pruned correctly — no unbounded disk growth.

## Side findings

- ~105 `git remote -v` processes, 5 days old, orphaned to launchd on your machine. **Not brain's code** (it never runs `remote -v`; its runner is leak-safe) — they match agent-transcript commands, so some agent harness is leaking them. Worth a `pkill -f 'git remote -v'`.
- `refresh --agent none` exits 1 on a dirty worktree with the error only on stderr — in scripts it looks like a silent failure; needs `--worktree`.
- Not tested (interactive/mutating/needs-agent): `distill`, `publish`, `webhook`, `dash`, `viz`, `watch`, `setup` daemon install, `facts sync`/`proposals`.

**Biggest wins by effort:** wire the existing metadata cache into status/verify/entities (near one-line, kills most of #1/#5) and gate delta's hashing on size+mtime (kills #3). Those two alone take the worst everyday paths from ~45–70s to roughly nothing.
